findings.title: Org and team ANY conditions are never executed against the database
findings.body: The only test that executes SQL through $queryRaw uses scope "user", which produces no array parameter. The org and team authorization tests only compare Prisma.Sql objects with toEqual, so they verify the stored strings/values but not that PostgreSQL and Prisma accept and correctly bind `= ANY(${numberArray})` at runtime. If array serialization or parameter typing fails for ANY, every org/team insights query would fail in production while these tests pass; an executed org or team $queryRaw case is needed.

findings.title: Single event-type filter returns an unparenthesized OR expression
findings.body: When eventTypeId is the only filter, buildFilterConditions returns `("eventTypeId" = ...) OR ("eventParentId" = ...)` with no outer parentheses. The previous Prisma WhereInput preserved this OR as a grouped unit in any composition. Now, any caller that composes the public getFilterConditions() result as `... AND ${filter}` gets `( ... AND eventTypeId = ...) OR eventParentId = ...` due to AND/OR precedence, potentially returning bookings matching eventParentId outside the intended preceding conditions. getBaseConditions happens to wrap it, but the standalone filter condition is unsafe and inconsistent with the combined-filter case, which does add parentheses.

findings.title: Public options type allows a team scope without teamId
findings.body: InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions makes teamId optional for every scope, so `{ scope: "team", userId, orgId }` now compiles. The runtime schema then rejects it, stores options as null, and all queries silently return the 1=0 condition instead of the caller getting a compile-time error as with the previous discriminated-union options type. This turns a programming error into silently empty insights data.

findings.title: Caching behavior lost its test coverage
findings.body: The service still caches authorization and filter conditions (cachedAuthConditions/cachedFilterConditions at lines 49-50 and the checks at lines 84-94), but this PR deletes the previous "Caching" describe block from the integration tests and adds no replacement. A regression that stops returning the cached Prisma.Sql, rebuilds conditions on every call, or mishandles the cached null filter result would no longer be detected.
